annotation_note: LPA encodes apolipoprotein(a), the defining component of lipoprotein(a) and a canonical pleiotropic cardiovascular risk gene. Human genetics links higher lipoprotein(a) to coronary disease and supports effects across peripheral vascular disease, stroke, heart failure and aortic stenosis, making this locus a model of shared cardiovascular biology.

CDKN2B labels the 9p21.3 locus, one of the most replicated pleiotropic vascular-risk regions, associated across coronary disease, ischaemic stroke, peripheral arterial disease and abdominal aortic aneurysm. Functional studies connect reduced CDKN2B activity to vascular smooth-muscle proliferation and apoptosis, defective efferocytosis and growth of complex atherosclerotic plaques.

FES is the best-supported effector at the 15q26.1 coronary locus: CAD-risk variants reduce FES expression in monocytes, while experimental FES depletion promotes monocyte and vascular smooth-muscle migration and loss of Fes accelerates atherosclerosis. FURIN is also a CTAS-significant member and an established blood-pressure locus, making this a vascular region with two credible cardiovascular genes.

APOE is a canonical pleiotropic lipid and vascular-risk gene. Its epsilon2/epsilon3/epsilon4 isoforms alter remnant-lipoprotein clearance and show graded relationships with LDL cholesterol, carotid atherosclerosis, coronary risk and ischaemic stroke, linking a fundamental lipid-transport mechanism to disease across vascular beds.

MARK3 encodes a kinase involved in cell polarity and metabolic control, and human genetics links the region to hypertension. The same CTAS locus contains BAG5, for which rare loss-of-function variants and experimental rescue studies provide direct evidence in dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia and cardiac calcium-handling biology.

CFDP1 is the CTAS representative at the BCAR1-CFDP1-TMEM170A atherosclerosis locus. The lead variant lies within CFDP1 and associates with carotid intima-media thickness, plaque burden and coronary risk, while vascular eQTL and functional analyses prioritise nearby BCAR1 as a leading regional effector candidate.

The gene-dense MHC/6p21 interval is an established immune-vascular region with genome-wide-significant association to coronary disease. ATP6V1G2 is the CTAS representative of this 32-gene locus; extended linkage disequilibrium means that the cardiovascular evidence belongs to the region rather than to a single resolved effector.

ZNF652 encodes a transcriptional repressor and marks one of the first robust common-variant blood-pressure loci. Variants near ZNF652 associate with systolic and diastolic pressure and with hypertension, establishing this as a pressure-regulation locus even though the downstream transcriptional mechanism remains unresolved.

CARF is the CTAS representative at the 2q33 WDR12 locus. Variants in this region were discovered and replicated at genome-wide significance for early-onset myocardial infarction; WDR12, a ribosome-biogenesis factor and CTAS-significant member, supplies the established cardiovascular context, while the effector mechanism remains unresolved.

CELSR2 labels the canonical 1p13 lipid-coronary locus, strongly associated with LDL cholesterol and myocardial infarction. Functional genetics identifies nearby SORT1 as the principal regional effector: the causal non-coding variant changes hepatic SORT1 expression, VLDL secretion and circulating LDL. SORT1 provides regional context but is not a CTAS-significant member of this locus.

ACAD10 is the CTAS representative of the highly pleiotropic 12q24 locus. Its CTAS-significant members include SH2B3 (LNK), an adaptor protein that restrains cytokine and growth-factor signalling in blood and vascular cells, and common variation across this dense interval tracks with blood pressure. CTAS ranks it among the strongest cross-cardiovascular signals.

HNF1A encodes a transcription factor central to hepatic and pancreatic-islet gene programmes; rare coding mutations cause maturity-onset diabetes of the young, while regulatory variation shapes C-reactive protein, LDL cholesterol and coronary artery disease. This is an established metabolic–coronary locus rather than an incidental signal.

IREB2 is the statistical representative at 15q25.1, but the locus's established cardiovascular effector is ADAMTS7, a secreted metalloprotease that drives vascular smooth-muscle migration and neointima formation and is a replicated coronary-artery-disease gene. IREB2 itself sets cellular iron homeostasis through iron-responsive-element binding.

TBX20 encodes a T-box transcription factor essential for cardiac chamber, valve and outflow-tract development. Rare mutations cause congenital heart defects and dilated cardiomyopathy, and continued expression maintains adult myocardial structure, marking this as a developmental heart locus.

DALRD3 is the statistical representative of the gene-dense 3p21.31 interval, whose CTAS-significant members include RHOA, a master GTPase controlling actin dynamics and vascular smooth-muscle contraction. Common variation across this region is associated with coronary artery disease.

ORMDL3 gates de novo sphingolipid synthesis by regulating serine palmitoyltransferase, a pathway increasingly tied to vascular inflammation. Experimental studies implicate ORMDL3 in atherosclerosis, and CTAS foregrounds this 17q21 locus across cardiovascular traits.

CFHR3 belongs to the complement factor-H-related cluster at 1q31.3 and tunes activation of the alternative complement pathway. This is a genuinely emerging cardiovascular locus: CTAS supplies the cross-trait prioritisation, with no established prior effector yet assigned.

C6orf106 (ILRUN) regulates innate-immune and lipid-related transcription and indexes the 6p21.31 locus. The region, which also carries UHRF1BP1, is associated with coronary artery disease in genome-wide studies.

HTRA1 encodes a secreted serine protease that remodels the extracellular matrix and restrains TGF-beta signalling in the vessel wall. Loss-of-function causes CARASIL and milder variants drive cerebral small-vessel disease and stroke, making this a Mendelian small-vessel locus with cross-cardiovascular reach.

LDLR encodes the hepatic LDL receptor that clears circulating LDL cholesterol; loss-of-function mutations cause familial hypercholesterolaemia and both rare and common variants raise LDL and myocardial-infarction risk. This is one of the canonical genes of coronary atherosclerosis.

LPL encodes lipoprotein lipase, the enzyme that hydrolyses triglyceride-rich lipoprotein cores at the endothelial surface. Genetic variation in LPL is a well-established determinant of plasma triglycerides and coronary artery disease, anchoring the triglyceride arm of cardiovascular risk.

PPAP2B (PLPP3) is a canonical coronary locus. The gene encodes a plasma-membrane lipid phosphatase that degrades pro-inflammatory lysophosphatidic acid in endothelium and smooth muscle, and its common variants are robustly associated with coronary artery disease independent of classical lipids.

SMG6 is the statistical representative of the 17p13.1 coronary locus; the lead signal in this interval is a replicated coronary-artery-disease association whose effector remains debated between SMG6 and neighbouring SRR. SMG6 itself is a nuclease of the nonsense-mediated-decay pathway.

ZFPM2 (FOG2) encodes a GATA-family transcriptional cofactor essential for cardiac morphogenesis and coronary-vessel formation from epicardium. The locus is associated with atrial fibrillation, and its developmental role connects it to structural as well as arrhythmic phenotypes.

NME7 represents the 1q24.2 locus, which also contains ATP1B1, the Na+/K+-ATPase beta-subunit governing vascular ion transport and blood pressure. The interval also lies adjacent to the neighbouring F5 coagulation gene, which carries a distinct genome-wide association with venous thromboembolism at this cytoband.

COL4A1 encodes the alpha-1 chain of type IV collagen, a core structural component of vascular and glomerular basement membranes. Mutations cause a Mendelian small-vessel arteriopathy with cerebral haemorrhage and stroke, giving this locus a defined role in vessel-wall integrity.

DYM (dymeclin) organises the Golgi apparatus and is the CTAS statistical representative at 18q21.1. The region carries an older blood-pressure linkage signal whose responsible gene is unresolved; CTAS re-prioritises it across cardiovascular traits.

PCCB encodes the beta subunit of propionyl-CoA carboxylase, a mitochondrial enzyme of branched-chain amino-acid and odd-chain fatty-acid catabolism whose deficiency causes propionic acidaemia with cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia. Functional and genetic work links this metabolic locus to cardiovascular phenotypes.

MIA3 (TANGO1) controls endoplasmic-reticulum export of bulky cargoes such as collagens and is the established gene at this 1q41 locus, identified in early genome-wide studies of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.

ARHGEF12 (LARG) is a RhoA guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor that couples G-protein-coupled receptors to vascular smooth-muscle contraction. The 11q23.3 interval it indexes is a coronary-artery-disease locus.

KCNH2 (hERG) forms the rapid delayed-rectifier potassium channel that repolarises the cardiac action potential. Loss-of-function mutations cause long-QT syndrome type 2 with risk of ventricular arrhythmia and sudden death, making this a canonical cardiac-repolarisation locus.

ZNF471 represents a 19q13.43 zinc-finger-gene cluster; its CTAS-significant members ZFP28 and ZNF470 are associated with cardiovascular traits in genome-wide studies. The specific effector is unresolved, and CTAS treats this as a cross-trait signal within a transcription-factor region.

PTK2 (FAK) is a focal-adhesion kinase that transduces mechanical and integrin signals in cardiomyocytes and vascular cells, governing adhesion, migration and hypertrophic remodelling. The locus is associated with atrial fibrillation, linking a mechanotransduction pathway to arrhythmia.

ABO encodes the glycosyltransferase that builds the A and B blood-group antigens and, through them, sets circulating levels of von Willebrand factor and factor VIII. It is a classical determinant of venous thromboembolism and broader thrombotic risk.

PHACTR1 regulates protein phosphatase-1 and actin dynamics in the vessel wall and marks one of the most pleiotropic arterial loci in the genome. Its variants are firmly associated with cervical artery dissection and fibromuscular dysplasia alongside coronary artery disease.

CYTH1 (cytohesin-1) activates ARF GTPases controlling integrin signalling and vesicle traffic in immune and vascular cells. The 17q25.3 region it indexes is associated with atrial fibrillation in genome-wide studies.

CDKN1A (p21) is a cyclin-dependent-kinase inhibitor that enforces cell-cycle arrest and modulates vascular smooth-muscle and cardiomyocyte proliferation. The locus is associated with atrial fibrillation, connecting cell-cycle control to arrhythmia susceptibility.

XPO7 is the CTAS representative of a 8p21 locus associated with atrial fibrillation; the region also contains DOK2, an adaptor that dampens tyrosine-kinase signalling. XPO7 itself is a broad-specificity nuclear-export receptor.

MMP16 is a membrane-type matrix metalloproteinase that activates other MMPs and remodels the extracellular matrix of the vessel wall. The locus is associated with blood pressure in genome-wide studies, consistent with a role in vascular structure.

IL6R encodes the interleukin-6 receptor, a central node of vascular inflammation. Genetic variation at IL6R is associated with coronary artery disease and supports the IL-6 pathway as a causal, druggable target in atherosclerosis.

CLDN23 represents the 8p23.1 locus; its CTAS-significant members include SOX7, an endothelial transcription factor guiding vascular development, and MSRA. The region is associated with blood pressure, with SOX7 the leading vascular candidate.

FBRSL1, an AUTS2-family transcriptional regulator, indexes the 12q24.33 locus, which is associated with blood pressure in genome-wide studies. The effector biology is only partly resolved, and CTAS ranks the interval as a cross-trait pressure signal.

GTF2I lies in the Williams-Beuren region at 7q11.23; its CTAS-significant members include NCF1, a subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase that shapes vascular oxidative stress. The region is associated with atrial fibrillation and blood pressure.

GRK4 phosphorylates and desensitises dopaminergic and other G-protein-coupled receptors in the renal tubule, a mechanism long tied to salt handling and hypertension. The 4p16.3 locus it marks is associated with blood pressure.

annotation_sources.label: Felder 2002 (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A)

annotation_note: HOXD13 is a homeodomain transcription factor patterning the developing limb and body axis. This is a genuinely emerging cardiovascular locus at 2q31.1, brought forward by CTAS cross-trait prioritisation without a previously established effector.

MRAS encodes a Ras-family GTPase that transduces growth-factor signalling in vascular cells and is the established gene at this 3q22 coronary locus, identified and replicated in genome-wide studies of coronary artery disease.

APOA5 encodes apolipoprotein A-V, a potent activator of lipoprotein-lipase-mediated triglyceride clearance. Coding and regulatory variants raise plasma triglycerides and myocardial-infarction risk, placing this locus firmly in the triglyceride–coronary axis.

HIBADH encodes mitochondrial 3-hydroxyisobutyrate dehydrogenase in the valine-catabolism pathway and shares this 7p15 locus with the HOXA gene cluster. The interval is associated with blood pressure, and CTAS prioritises it as a metabolic–pressure signal.

ENSA encodes alpha-endosulfine, an inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A that also couples metabolic state to KATP-channel activity. This is an emerging 1q21.3 locus surfaced by CTAS cross-cardiovascular prioritisation rather than a previously reported effector.

EFR3B represents a 2p23.3 locus whose CTAS-significant members include ADCY3, an adenylate cyclase linked to adiposity and cardiometabolic traits. The region is associated with blood pressure, with ADCY3 the leading metabolic candidate.

SMAD3 is an intracellular transducer of TGF-beta signalling essential for vessel-wall homeostasis. Loss-of-function mutations cause aneurysms-osteoarthritis syndrome with aortic aneurysm and dissection, defining a Mendelian aortopathy locus.

CCDC90B (MCUB) is a dominant-negative subunit of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter that tunes mitochondrial calcium uptake, a process important for cardiac energetics. CTAS prioritises this 11q14.1 locus as an emerging cross-trait signal.

EXD2 encodes a mitochondrial 3'-5' exonuclease influencing translation and mitochondrial function, and indexes the 14q24.1 locus that harbours the coronary candidate ZFP36L1. GWAS place a coronary-artery-disease signal in the region.

EDNRA encodes the endothelin-A receptor, the principal mediator of endothelin-1 vasoconstriction and a validated antihypertensive drug target. Its locus is associated with blood pressure and coronary artery disease, tying a core vasoconstrictor pathway to disease.

DUSP13 is the statistical representative at 10q22.3; the cardiovascular signal in this region belongs to the neighbouring KCNMA1, which encodes the large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel controlling vascular tone. KCNMA1 sits just outside CTAS membership as regional context.

RASIP1 encodes an endothelial-specific Ras-interacting protein required for vascular lumen formation and endothelial barrier integrity. Its 17q25 locus, which also contains FUT2, is associated with blood pressure, making RASIP1 a strong vascular candidate.

CENPW is the representative at 6q22.32; the established cardiovascular gene nearby is RSPO3, a WNT-pathway modulator associated with blood pressure and pulse pressure. CENPW itself is a kinetochore-assembly factor and RSPO3 provides the regional context.

DUS4L represents the 7q22.3 locus, whose CTAS-significant members include COG5 and BCAP29; the region carries a replicated coronary-artery-disease association. The individual effector is unresolved, and CTAS treats this as a coronary-region signal.

VAMP8 (endobrevin) is the primary v-SNARE driving platelet granule secretion, a step central to haemostasis and thrombosis. It represents the 2p11.2 locus — which also contains the vitamin-K-dependent carboxylase GGCX — where genome-wide studies place a coronary-artery-disease association.

GLI1 marks a gene-rich 12q13.3 locus; its CTAS-significant members include LRP1, a large endocytic receptor with broad roles in vascular-wall biology and an established human-genetic association with abdominal aortic aneurysm. LRP1 is the leading cardiovascular effector here, with GLI1 the statistical representative.

TMEM8B indexes the 9p13.3 locus, which also contains GBA2; the interval is associated with atrial fibrillation in genome-wide studies. The specific effector is unresolved, and CTAS ranks it as a cross-trait arrhythmia signal.

SMC6 forms part of the SMC5/6 genome-maintenance complex and indexes the 2p24.3 locus, which is associated with blood-lipid levels in genome-wide studies. This is an emerging cross-trait signal rather than an established cardiovascular gene.

OBFC1 (STN1) supports telomere replication and is the representative at 10q24.33; the region's established cardiovascular genes are the neighbouring CNNM2 and NT5C2, associated with blood pressure. These sit just outside CTAS membership as regional context.

TIPARP is a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase that regulates aryl-hydrocarbon-receptor and metabolic signalling, and represents the 3q25.31 locus containing LEKR1, associated with cardiac and growth phenotypes. CTAS prioritises the interval across cardiovascular traits.

B3GNT2 builds poly-N-acetyllactosamine chains on cell-surface glycoproteins and represents a 2p15 locus that also contains PUS10; the region is associated with atrial fibrillation. The effector remains unresolved.

NCOA5 is a nuclear-receptor coregulator with dual coactivator and corepressor activity affecting oestrogen- and metabolic-receptor signalling. CTAS brings this 20q13.12 locus forward as an emerging cross-cardiovascular signal.

CRIM1 encodes a transmembrane BMP and growth-factor modulator expressed in endothelium and important for vascular development. Its locus is associated with atrial fibrillation, linking developmental vascular signalling to arrhythmia.

HDGFL1 is a poorly characterised PWWP-domain nuclear protein indexing the 6p22.3 locus, which carries a coronary-artery-disease association in genome-wide studies. CTAS prioritises the interval as a coronary-region signal with an unresolved effector.

ENPEP encodes glutamyl aminopeptidase (aminopeptidase A), which converts angiotensin II to angiotensin III in central blood-pressure control and is an antihypertensive drug target. The same CTAS locus contains PITX2, the principal transcription-factor gene of atrial fibrillation, making this 4q25 interval one with two distinct cardiovascular effectors.

GCK encodes glucokinase, the glucose sensor governing insulin secretion and hepatic glucose handling; its coding mutations cause monogenic diabetes. The 7p13 locus is associated with blood-lipid and glycaemic traits, and CTAS prioritises it across cardiometabolic phenotypes.

GGT7 metabolises glutathione conjugates and regulates cellular redox balance, indexing the 20q11.22 locus that also contains TP53INP2. The 20q11.22 region carries a coronary-artery-disease association.
CEP68 is a centrosomal linker protein maintaining centrosome cohesion, and its locus is associated with atrial fibrillation in genome-wide studies. CTAS ranks it among cross-trait arrhythmia signals.

EIF5A is a translation factor, uniquely modified by hypusination, that resolves ribosome stalling. This is an emerging 17p13.1 cardiovascular locus surfaced by CTAS cross-trait prioritisation rather than a previously established gene.
MAP2K6 (MKK6) activates p38 MAPK stress signalling in cardiomyocytes, a pathway central to cardiac remodelling. The locus is associated with heart failure in genome-wide studies.

annotation_sources.label: Liao 2001 (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A)

annotation_note: KDF1 regulates epidermal progenitor proliferation in development and indexes the 1p36.11 locus, which is associated with blood pressure in genome-wide studies. The cardiovascular effector is unresolved.

RPP14 is a subunit of ribonuclease P that processes precursor tRNAs. This is a genuinely emerging 3p14.3 locus prioritised by CTAS across cardiovascular traits, without a previously reported effector gene.

MARCH2 encodes a membrane-anchored E3 ubiquitin ligase controlling trafficking and turnover of cell-surface receptors. Functional studies implicate MARCH2 in protection against myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion injury, giving this locus experimental cardiovascular relevance.

FGD5 is a RhoGEF that activates CDC42 in endothelial cells to control angiogenesis and vascular sprouting. Its locus is associated with coronary artery disease and blood pressure, consistent with an endothelial mechanism.
KIZ (kizuna) stabilises the mitotic spindle pole. This is an emerging 20p11.23 locus associated with atrial fibrillation in genome-wide studies, prioritised by CTAS across cardiovascular traits.
MDH1 encodes cytosolic malate dehydrogenase of the malate-aspartate shuttle, linking cytosolic and mitochondrial metabolism. Its 2p15 locus carries a coronary-artery-disease signal.

ARHGAP42 is a RhoA GTPase-activating protein expressed in vascular smooth muscle that sets basal vascular tone and blood pressure; a causal regulatory variant lowering ARHGAP42 raises pressure. This is a functionally supported blood-pressure locus.

DOC2A is a calcium-sensing regulator of vesicle fusion and indexes the 16p11.2 locus alongside FAM57B. This is an emerging cardiovascular signal from CTAS cross-trait prioritisation, with no established prior effector at the interval.

NADK phosphorylates NAD+ to NADP+, setting the cytosolic NADP(H) pool that supports redox defence and biosynthesis, and represents the 1p36 locus containing the aortopathy gene SKI. The region is associated with blood pressure.
ESPL1 (separase) cleaves cohesin to trigger sister-chromatid separation at anaphase. CTAS surfaces this 12q13.13 locus as an emerging cross-cardiovascular signal rather than an established gene.

NMRK1 encodes nicotinamide-riboside kinase 1, an entry enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway relevant to cardiac and vascular energetics. This is an emerging 9q21.13 locus brought forward by CTAS cross-trait prioritisation.
KCNK5 (TASK-2) is a two-pore-domain potassium channel controlling membrane potential in vascular and renal cells. GWAS place a coronary-artery-disease signal at its locus.

KCNK4 (TRAAK) is a mechanosensitive two-pore-domain potassium channel gated by membrane stretch and temperature. CTAS prioritises this 11q13.1 locus as an emerging cross-cardiovascular signal, without a previously established effector.
UPF3A is a component of the nonsense-mediated-decay pathway and indexes the 13q34 locus, which is associated with blood pressure in genome-wide studies. The specific effector is unresolved.

TAF4 is a subunit of the TFIID complex that nucleates RNA-polymerase-II pre-initiation. This is a genuinely emerging 20q13.33 cardiovascular locus, prioritised by CTAS across traits without a previously established effector.

NUMBL is an endocytic adaptor regulating NOTCH signalling and cell-fate decisions. This is an emerging 19q13.2 cardiovascular locus from CTAS cross-trait prioritisation, without a previously reported effector.
RGS7BP anchors R7-family regulators of G-protein signalling at the membrane, tuning GPCR responses in neurovascular tissue. Its locus is associated with blood pressure in genome-wide studies.
